core.title: Convert slugs and filesystem names by swapping hyphens and underscores
core.given: A plan artifact needs a wagon or feature slug or its filesystem counterpart (wagon directory name or feature file name).
core.when: Deriving a slug from a name, or converting between a slug and its directory/file name in either direction.
core.then: Use only the canonical conversions: derive slug = lowercase the name and replace spaces/underscores with hyphens; slug to directory name = replace hyphens with underscores; directory name to slug = replace underscores with hyphens; feature slug to file name = replace hyphens with underscores and append the plan-artifact file suffix; feature file name to slug = strip that suffix and replace underscores with hyphens.
prefer: Verb-object phrasing for slugs (preferred, not required).
avoid: Any other slug to/from filesystem-name transformation (abbreviating, reordering, dropping words).
Hyphens in wagon directory or feature file names; spaces, underscores or capitals in slugs.
Omitting or doubling the feature file suffix.
core.why: Logical slugs are kebab-case and filesystem names snake_case; the conversions are pure hyphen/underscore swaps between them.
evidence: For every wagon, replacing underscores with hyphens in its directory name equals its declared slug, and replacing hyphens with underscores in its slug equals its directory name.

For every feature, replacing hyphens with underscores in its slug and appending the plan-artifact file suffix equals its file name, and stripping that suffix and replacing underscores with hyphens equals its slug.
Every slug is lowercase with hyphens only (no spaces or underscores).
verification: Slug derivation enforcement split: lowercasing and replacing spaces/underscores with hyphens are mandatory; verb-object phrasing is advisory only — do not raise a finding on non-verb-object phrasing alone.

The check round-trips each wagon's slug with its directory name and each feature's slug with its file name (file suffix from the profile), and validates that every slug is lowercase with hyphens only; it does not cover the naming of files or directories that are not wagon directories or feature files.

Slug/dirname/filename pairing needs a diff-level observer that pairs a declared or referenced slug with its directory or feature file name and checks the mapping; no path restriction is applied — wagon/feature artifacts may live anywhere in the repository.

values: slug referenced alongside a directory or feature filename

fires: A new wagon is created whose kebab-case slug must become a snake_case directory name.
A feature is added whose slug must become a snake_case feature file name.
A slug is derived from a human wagon/feature name containing spaces, capitals or underscores, with or without creating any file.
An existing wagon directory or feature file name is read and its logical slug is referenced in a plan, URN or doc.
doesNotFire: Editing the content of an existing wagon or feature without touching, deriving or referencing its slug, directory or file name.
Naming files or directories that are not wagon directories or feature files (e.g. files of other roles such as source files).

profileRequirements.meaning: The file suffix that identifies a feature's plan (feature) file; it is appended to the slug-derived basename when naming the file and stripped when recovering the slug from the file name.

classification.note: 'planner artifact' becomes the plan_artifact role; the '.yaml' feature filename is named generically, with the suffix supplied by the profile.
The five conversions are stated neutrally; the '.yaml' literal is replaced by 'the plan-artifact file suffix' from the profile.
Verb-object phrasing is a naming style, not stack machinery; kept as advisory.
Neutral negative restatement of the conversion functions.
Character conventions (kebab slugs, snake names) are the convention itself and stay in the core.
'the .yaml suffix' becomes 'the feature file suffix', taken from the profile.
Round-trip restated in words; identical obligation.
Round-trip restated in words with the file suffix from the profile.

The term definition restates the general naming convention, not stack-specific APIs or implementation: the slug_to_dirname / dirname_to_slug / feature_slug_to_filename / feature_filename_to_slug / slug_derivation aliases and their hyphen/underscore string replacements duplicate the canonical conversions already in core.then; the only stack-dependent datum is the '.yaml' file-suffix literal, supplied by suffix.plan_artifact.
The mandatory/advisory split and 'do not fail on phrasing alone' are generic per-rule enforcement scope, kept in core.verification.
Task terms are ATDD naming vocabulary (slug, wagon, feature, dirname), not stack terms.
Change facts are neutral; the note's diff-level-observer requirement and 'no path restriction' deference are kept as a core.verification entry.

neutralityNotes: The convention is a naming policy, not stack machinery: the kebab-case/slash snake-case alphabets, the hyphen/underscore swaps, and the conversion-function aliases that name them are the obligation itself, so they remain in the core rather than the profile (no vocabulary key covers naming separators, and none is needed). The only stack-concrete datum is the feature-file suffix '.yaml' (suffix.plan_artifact). 'wagon' and 'feature' are ATDD plan-artifact concepts already carried by the profile vocabulary (layout.wagon_dir, layout.feature_dir, urn.wagon, urn.feature), so they are used as neutral terms. Per the activation change fact, the rule needs a new diff-level observer and applies no path restriction, which is stated in core.verification.
